title: Tau Ceti: A Nearby Sun-Like Star
fact: Tau Ceti is a G-type main-sequence star located about 11.9 light-years from Earth in the constellation Cetus. It is one of the closest solitary stars similar to our Sun.

title: Tau Ceti in Project Hail Mary
fact: In Andy Weir's 'Project Hail Mary' (and its 2026 film adaptation), Tau Ceti is the destination for Ryland Grace's mission. It features a planet called Adrian (Tau Ceti e) with life forms like Taumoeba that combat Astrophage.

title: Earth's Unique Liquid Water
fact: Earth is the only planet in our solar system with stable liquid water on its surface, covering about 71% of the planet, which enabled life to begin around 3.8 billion years ago.

title: The Sun: Our Average Star
fact: Every star visible to the naked eye in the night sky is bigger and brighter than our Sun, except for a few faint ones. The Sun appears bright due to its proximity.

title: Tau Ceti's Exoplanets
fact: Tau Ceti has multiple planet candidates, including several super-Earths. Tau Ceti e orbits in or near the habitable zone, though confirmation remains ongoing.

title: Earth's Protective Moon
fact: Earth's Moon formed from debris after a massive collision with a Mars-sized body early in its history. It stabilizes Earth's axial tilt, helping maintain stable climates.

title: Neutron Stars: Extreme Density
fact: A teaspoon of material from a neutron star would weigh about 10 billion tons on Earth due to their incredible density.

title: Milky Way Star Count
fact: Our Milky Way galaxy contains between 100 and 400 billion stars, vastly outnumbered by the estimated 3 trillion trees on Earth.

title: Tau Ceti Debris Disk
fact: Tau Ceti is surrounded by a massive debris disk with roughly ten times more dust and material than our Solar System's Kuiper Belt and asteroid belt combined.

title: Venus: Earth's Twin
fact: Venus is often called Earth's twin due to similar size and mass, but its extreme greenhouse effect makes it the hottest planet with surface temperatures over 460°C.

title: Stars as Element Forges
fact: Stars create heavier elements through nuclear fusion and supernovae. Neutron star mergers are key sites for producing gold, platinum, and other precious metals.

title: Jupiter: Solar System Giant
fact: Jupiter is so massive that all other planets combined wouldn't equal half its mass. It has at least 95 moons and acts as a gravitational shield for Earth.

title: Tau Ceti's Stability
fact: Unlike other stars affected by Astrophage in 'Project Hail Mary', Tau Ceti maintains its luminosity despite the fictional infection, highlighting its real-world stability as a G8V star.

title: Black Holes and Gravitational Waves
fact: The first detected gravitational waves in 2015 came from merging black holes, releasing energy equivalent to 50 times the power of all stars in the observable universe for a brief moment.

title: Earth's Magnetic Field
fact: Earth's molten outer core generates a magnetic field that protects the atmosphere from solar wind and cosmic radiation, enabling life to thrive.

title: Exoplanets Everywhere
fact: Astronomers estimate that nearly every star you see in the night sky has at least one planet orbiting it, with thousands of confirmed exoplanets to date.

title: Sun's True Color
fact: Our Sun is technically a green-blue star, peaking in that wavelength, but appears white/yellow from Earth due to atmospheric scattering.

title: Light-Year Scale
fact: One light-year is about 5.88 trillion miles. Tau Ceti is roughly 11.9 light-years away, making interstellar travel a massive challenge even at near-light speeds.

title: Earth's Rotation Slowdown
fact: Earth's rotation is gradually slowing due to tidal interactions with the Moon, lengthening days by about 1.7 milliseconds per century.

title: Universe's Vastness
fact: The observable universe contains an estimated 100 billion to 2 trillion galaxies, with more stars than grains of sand on all Earth's beaches combined.
